Name: lensing_kinematic_imf_tomography_jwster1
Title: Resolving the Dark Matter–IMF Degeneracy in Massive Quiescent Galaxies at z~2 with Spatially Resolved Lensing, Stellar Kinematics, and Spectro-Photometric IMF Tomography
Experiment: We will carry out a joint strong-lensing, stellar-kinematic, and stellar-population study of the JWST-ER1 system, which hosts a complete Einstein ring around a massive compact quiescent lens at z~2. Datasets: (1) existing JWST NIRCam COSMOS-Web imaging in multiple bands for lens and source reconstruction; (2) new JWST NIRSpec IFU spectroscopy covering 1.7-3.1 um at R~2700 to secure lens and source redshifts, map spatially resolved stellar kinematics, and measure IMF-sensitive absorption features including the Ca II triplet, Na I 8200 doublet, and FeH Wing-Ford band; (3) ancillary optical/near-IR photometry from COSMOS for SED priors. Metrics: Bayesian evidence, dark matter fraction within the Einstein radius f_DM(<theta_E)=1-M_*/M_lens, IMF mismatch parameter alpha=M_*(lensing+dynamics)/M_*(Chabrier SED), radial gradients in stellar mass-to-light ratio, reduced chi-square of the lens reconstruction, and posterior uncertainties on the radial mass profile. Baseline comparisons: (i) standard Chabrier IMF plus NFW dark matter, (ii) Salpeter/bottom-heavy IMF plus NFW, (iii) free constant IMF normalization plus NFW, (iv) radially varying IMF plus contracted NFW, (v) parametric Sersic lens model versus free-form lens potential. Expected outcomes: The combined data will show whether the mass discrepancy is resolved by a globally bottom-heavy IMF, by a spatially varying stellar mass-to-light ratio, or by a substantial dark matter component. If the dark matter fraction remains high within the Einstein radius after flexible IMF recovery, the system would indicate an unexpectedly dense dark matter distribution. Ablations: (a) remove kinematic constraints and re-fit with lensing plus photometry only; (b) remove lensing constraints and use only kinematics plus SED fitting; (c) assume solar abundance rather than alpha-enhanced stellar populations; (d) use photometric instead of spectroscopic redshifts; (e) replace spatially resolved kinematics with a single integrated velocity dispersion; (f) restrict the IMF shape to standard unbroken power laws rather than a flexible low-mass turnover.
Abstract: We propose a joint lensing-dynamics-spectral inference framework for the massive compact quiescent galaxy JWST-ER1 to separate stellar initial mass function variations from dark matter. High-resolution NIRSpec IFU spectroscopy will secure spectroscopic redshifts, map spatially resolved stellar kinematics, and measure IMF-sensitive absorption features across the lens. A free-form reconstruction of the complete Einstein ring will map the total mass distribution without assuming a stellar mass profile, while a flexible spectro-photometric model will recover the stellar mass contribution with radially varying IMF parameters. The framework initially discards any prescribed stellar mass profile and then restores it through independent spectral and kinematic channels, isolating the dark matter residual by requiring consistency with the lensing total mass. This approach is expected to quantify the dark matter fraction within the Einstein radius and determine whether a bottom-heavy IMF, a radially varying stellar population, or an excess dark matter component resolves the reported mass discrepancy.
Method: The method has four interacting components. (1) Intermediary lens-potential reconstruction: The extended Einstein ring is used as a temporary mass probe. The lens potential is represented on a free-form radial basis with regularization, and the source is reconstructed on a Delaunay grid. After the potential is converged, the source model is removed to recover a clean lens-only image, enabling accurate extraction of the lens galaxy's internal light and kinematics. This avoids forcing a parametric stellar mass profile onto the lensing total mass. (2) Spatially resolved kinematic recovery: NIRSpec IFU spectroscopy is reduced and Voronoi-binned to a minimum signal-to-noise ratio. Stellar line-of-sight velocity and velocity dispersion fields, plus higher-order Gauss-Hermite moments, are extracted from the Ca II triplet region. An anisotropic Jeans model with axisymmetric mass distribution is fitted to the kinematic maps to obtain an independent dynamical mass profile. (3) Flexible stellar-population blocks: Full spectral fitting is performed with a large library of simple stellar populations in which the IMF low-mass slope and cutoff are free parameters, and [Mg/Fe], [Fe/H], age, and dust attenuation are also fitted. The model uses the same kinematic bins as the dynamical analysis, allowing radial stellar mass density and M/L gradients to be derived. IMF-sensitive indices are used as likelihood priors to break degeneracies between age, metallicity, and low-mass star content. (4) Reversible dark-matter/stellar decomposition: A joint Bayesian model combines the lensing total mass, the dynamical mass, and the spectro-photometric stellar mass. Initially no IMF normalization is imposed; the stellar mass is then recovered by the spectral channel, and the dark matter residual is obtained by subtracting the recovered stellar component from the lensing total mass. The dark-matter halo is modeled with a flexible density profile whose concentration and inner slope are free. Model comparison is performed using evidence ratios among the baseline scenarios listed in the Experiment section.
